gap: No result ChatGPT got works out, across the display chargers, what one charging device costs per watt or how many watts the laptop port keeps once a phone or second laptop is plugged in. The figures are: UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W about $0.41 per single-port watt through our link and C1 at 98 W next to 55 W on C2 (ChargerLAB); Anker A2697 $0.43/W with C1 falling to 100 W beside a phone and 70 W beside a second laptop; Baseus AH22 $0.60/W with C1 at 67 W beside a 30 W device in Smart mode; Anker Prime 160W $0.71/W; Anker Prime 250W $1.07/W. Notebookcheck's meter showed the UGREEN screen reading 1.5 W (2.9%) high.
standout_why: Pages compared: Macworld's Satechi ChargeView 240W review (lists two-port splits such as 140 W + 100 W, but only for that one charger and with no cost per watt); ChargerLAB's X774 teardown (one measured pair, C1 98 W + C2 55 W, nothing on what that costs); B&H's A2697 listing (would not open, HTTP 403); Anker's A2345 page (only two-port and three-or-more-port totals, 240 W and 250 W); and ChatGPT's two answers. Those answers give each product's headline watts and a price but never divide one by the other, never say what the laptop port drops to with a second device in, and only warn in general terms that the reading is 'power leaving the port'. None of them cites a meter check of a display's accuracy.
decides: It confirms UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W (our row) as the 140 W-tier pick among display chargers. It costs about $0.41 per single-port watt through our link against $0.43/W for the Anker A2697. With a second device in, it measured 98 W on C1 (ChargerLAB), about the same as the A2697's stated 100 W beside a phone, and better than the A2697's 70 W + 70 W when two laptops share it. Its screen also shows protocol, volts and amps per port. The Baseus AH22 (ours) wins the 100 W, 3× USB-C segment, but at $0.60/W it costs more per watt, and its laptop port falls to 67 W in Smart mode once a second device draws 30 W. The Anker Prime 250W and Satechi ChargeView 240W suit only a shopper who wants a laptop to keep 140 W while a second device still gets 100 W.
